Subject: DPA: deployment-specific controls for Dedicated vs Private environments

Hi Jonas —

Thanks for the demo last week. Acme Health is interested in Redwood for our clinical insights pipeline, but before procurement can move forward we need a DPA that explicitly covers two things: (1) how data is handled for Dedicated (Redwood-managed GPU pools) vs Private/VPC/on‑prem deployments, and (2) the subprocessor and key management model when customers use our own KMS.

Two immediate asks:
- Can you send the current subprocessor matrix and indicate which subprocessors would be in the data path for Dedicated vs Private (we want to understand any cloud services that would touch PHI).
- We have a redline to your standard DPA (attached) that adds deployment-specific clauses and a narrow audit right for on‑prem. Please confirm if Redwood will accept or counter. We prefer DocuSign execution.

Attachment: Acme_DPA_Redline_v3.docx (redline to Redwood DPA)

Appreciate a short call if you think that helps — procurement wants signed paperwork before the end of the month.

Best,

Hi Olivia —

Thanks for the clear note and the redline. We're excited to work with Acme. Quick answers up front: we can provide the subprocessor matrix (see preliminary list below) and we support customer-controlled KMS for Private/VPC deployments; there are a few integration details to confirm on key wrapping and HSM access.

Preliminary subprocessors (high level):
- Cloud infra (compute/runtime) — used for Redwood Hosted and Dedicated control plane
- Metrics/logging provider — does not receive unredacted prompt/response data for Private deployments when customer requests isolation
- Model distribution mirror (CDN) — read-only model artifacts

Next steps from our side:
1) Legal will review your redline and propose counter-terms if needed (cc: Karthik).
2) Engineering (cc: Mina) will document the KMS/HSM integration points and expected data flows for Dedicated vs Private.
3) I'll prepare a DocuSign packet once we have an agreed redline.

Can we do a 30-minute sync Wednesday to walk the redlines? Please let me know a time that works.

Subject: Re: DPA: deployment-specific controls for Dedicated vs Private environments

Jonas —

Thanks for the quick reply. We attached a redline that: (a) requires Redwood to disclose subprocessors in-scope for a given deployment mode within 10 business days of contract signature; (b) adds a deployment appendix that clarifies data flow and encryption responsibilities for Dedicated vs Private; and (c) requests a limited audit right for on‑prem (one scheduled audit per year, scoped to controls around data segregation).

We flagged two specific items we consider non‑negotiable:
- Explicit responsibility for key custody when Acme uses our KMS in a Private deployment (Acme must retain sole control over keys; Redwood should not retain emergency access unless explicitly requested and documented).
- Subprocessor notification window: 10 business days prior to onboarding any new subprocessors that would touch Acme customer data in Dedicated deployments.

Attachment: Acme_DPA_Redline_v3.docx (redline)

If you prefer, legal can join the Wednesday sync.

Best,
Olivia

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redline (Acme) — suggested positions

Team —

I reviewed Acme's redline. High level suggestions:
- Key custody: We can accept language that permits customer-controlled KMS for Private/VPC and on‑prem; we must be explicit that for Dedicated (Redwood-managed) deployments the default is Redwood-managed keys unless the customer purchases a dedicated KMS connector add-on. We should offer an operational exception for emergency key rotation only with customer approval.
- Subprocessor notification: 10 business days is reasonable for major changes; we should push back on notification for non-data-path infra upgrades. Proposed counter: Redwood will notify customers of any subprocessor change that will have access to customer data or the ability to decrypt telemetry, with a 10-business-day notice for Dedicated and immediate notice plus a technical summary for Private (where applicable).
- Audit right: we should accept a narrow, scheduled audit for on‑prem (customer-hosted) only; for Dedicated/Hosted offer SOC2 reports and an on-site equivalent upon reasonable notice for enterprise customers.

Mina: can you confirm the data path specifics for Dedicated vs Private (KMS handshake, where logs are stored, and whether model caching touches cleartext)? I want to include concise bullets we can share with Acme.

Thanks,
Karthik
General Counsel (acting) | Redwood Inference

Hi Olivia —

Thanks for your patience while we reviewed the redline. We've agreed the following positions after legal and engineering review:
- Customer-controlled KMS: Accepted for Private/VPC/on‑prem. Redwood will not retain keys or emergency access unless explicitly requested and agreed in writing; we will document the key exchange and emergency procedures in the deployment appendix.
- Subprocessor notification: Accepted with the caveat that notifications will be for subprocessors with access to customer data or decryption ability. For Dedicated deployments we will provide 10 business days notice; for Private deployments we will provide immediate notification and a technical summary. Non-data-path infra changes will not trigger the 10-day notice.
- Audit: Limited, scheduled on‑prem audit accepted (one per year) scoped to data segregation controls. For Dedicated/Hosted, Acme may rely on Redwood's SOC 2 + complementary evidence.

Attached: Subprocessor_Matrix.csv; DocuSign_Acme_DPA_2026.pdf (DocuSign packet preview).

DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/Signing/?s=EXAMPLExxx

3) I'll share a short appendix summarizing the data flows for Dedicated vs Private (encryption at rest, where logs are stored, and KV cache behavior).

If anything urgent, loop legal on legal@acmehealth.com and I'll have Karthik follow up. Hoping we can close this week.
